nodes.label: Code is read ten times more often than written
nodes.rationale: The governing principle above every other rule: write for the person opening the file a year from now with no memory of it. Formatting is out of scope - .clang-format handles it automatically.

nodes.label: Naming convention (snake_case / PascalCase / UPPER_CASE / trailing _)
nodes.rationale: A name says what a thing is, not what type it is; the trailing underscore on private fields immediately distinguishes object state from a local. Units belong in the name (timeout_ms, lap_time_seconds) because that is cheap and kills a whole class of bugs.

nodes.label: RAII
nodes.rationale: The foundation of memory safety here: a resource opened in an object is released in its destructor even when an error occurs, so nobody has to remember to close it.

nodes.label: Smart pointers over raw pointers
nodes.rationale: unique_ptr by default (exactly one owner), shared_ptr only when there really are several owners because it costs more, raw T* only as a non-owning view that is never deleted. Manual new/delete leaks whenever an exception escapes between them.

nodes.label: Explicit ownership in design
nodes.rationale: For every object you must be able to say who owns it and when it dies; if you cannot answer, the design is not ready and it is too early to write code.

nodes.label: GPU resources need their own RAII wrapper
nodes.rationale: Smart pointers do not manage OpenGL textures and buffers, so they are wrapped in a class whose constructor calls glGen* and destructor glDelete*; this directly closes video-memory leaks.

nodes.label: Expected failures return optional / expected
nodes.rationale: A corrupt packet, a missing GPS fix or an unreachable server is normal life, not an exception. Returning std::optional/std::expected forces the caller to check, whereas a sentinel like -1 silently flows into the calculation.

nodes.label: Exceptions caught at module boundaries
nodes.rationale: Exceptions are allowed in the desktop client and track_server, but they are caught at module boundaries so one broken packet is logged and dropped instead of killing the process. The module boundary is a wall: an error inside the packet parser becomes an optional/expected or is caught there.

nodes.label: Validate inputs at the public entry point
nodes.rationale: A public function checks its arguments first (buffer length before reading, non-null pointers) so the rest of the code can trust its data.

nodes.label: Minimal header surface
nodes.rationale: Only what is actually used from outside goes in the .hpp; the less that is exposed, the freer the internals are to change without breaking callers.

nodes.label: DataSource abstraction (ServerSource / LocalReceiverSource)
nodes.rationale: The rest of the code works against DataSource and never learns which concrete source is underneath, so adding a third source is a new class and nothing else changes.

nodes.label: Unidirectional dependency arrows
nodes.rationale: rajagp_core knows nothing about client or track_server; both depend on core but not on each other, and there are no cycles. The moment core needs to know something about the client, the design has slipped.

nodes.label: One function, one job
nodes.rationale: A function doing three things cannot be reused or tested; the tell is that you cannot name it with one verb, or the name wants an 'and' (parse_and_send).

nodes.label: Comments explain why, not what
nodes.rationale: What the code does is visible in the code - if it is not, rewrite the code rather than adding a comment. Every public function carries a short block: what it does, takes, returns, and what happens on error.

nodes.label: TODO / FIXME / HACK markers
nodes.rationale: Uniform, greppable labels so both humans and AI agents can find unfinished work: TODO = finish later, FIXME = works but badly, HACK = temporary crutch with the reason spelled out.

nodes.label: spdlog level policy
nodes.rationale: trace/debug off in release, info for life events, warn when work continues anyway, error for a failed operation, critical when the program cannot go on. Never log per-frame or per-packet in a hot loop - it drowns the signal and costs speed. Log events, not the stream.

nodes.label: Shared data must be protected
nodes.rationale: Any variable written by one thread and read by another is either behind a std::mutex or passed through a thread-safe queue; there is no such thing as a merely shared variable between threads.

nodes.label: Prefer a queue to a mutex
nodes.rationale: The network thread puts a finished snapshot in a queue and the render thread takes it, so the threads never touch the same memory at once - races are impossible by construction, which is cleaner than sprinkling mutexes. Locks that do exist are held as briefly as possible, never across heavy work.

nodes.label: OpenGL calls only from the context thread
nodes.rationale: Every gl* call happens on the thread that created the context; the network thread never touches GL.

nodes.label: const by default, careful auto, named constants
nodes.rationale: const tells the reader nothing changes here; auto only where the type is obvious from the right-hand side; magic numbers become named constants (len < PACKET_SIZE_BYTES); variables are initialised at declaration because uninitialised ones cause bugs that are hard to catch.
